clue.text: Outside cover of old magazine, nothing inside

indicators.note: inside means the nought is placed within the magazine's title

parts.note: She was a British women's monthly magazine, now defunct
zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A collector complains that an old magazine's cover is all there is: the pages are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts O within SHE, the name of a former British women's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is the protective outer covering worn over the foot, and a horse has an iron one too.

clue.text: Muzzle tiny pup, now go shaking tails furiously

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild agitation, so the remaining letters are jumbled
shaking off the tails means each of the four words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An owner muzzles a small puppy that is wagging its tail madly before a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking tails' strips the last letter from tiny, pup, now and go, leaving TIN PU NO G; 'furiously' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held at the business end of a weapon, its muzzle pointed at you, is being held at this.

clue.text: Do well to make 4 go into 3? Not quite

indicators.note: go into means the numeral is placed inside the other word
not quite means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the number three written out as a word
four in Roman numerals is IV

explanation.surface: A puzzled arithmetic question: how can four possibly fit into three?
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are words, not quantities: 4 is the Roman numeral and 3 the written word, minus its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or prosper is to do well; the verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Legal fellow's 33% orange since being shaken up

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is its first two letters
shaken up means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer's portion of an orange gets shaken up somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: '33%' takes the first third of ORANGE, OR; 'being shaken up' rearranges SINCE to ENSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes science or evidence used in courts of law, so it means relating to legal matters.

clue.text: Many stars party and kiss everybody at the end

parts.note: a gala is a festive party or celebration
X is the conventional kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: at the end means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A star-studded party where everyone kisses at the close of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge system of countless stars bound by gravity, like the Milky Way.

clue.text: Tend to be troubled by depression?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone prone to getting upset when feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like the mood, but it is a hollow in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hollow pressed into a surface, as on a car door, is a depression.

clue.text: Doctor to hug feet of each patient? It's an idea

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered in order
the feet of words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A doctor considering hugging every patient: is that a good idea?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges TO HUG into THOUG; 'feet of' takes H and T from each and patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or something conceived in the mind is a synonym for an idea.

clue.text: One looking for a geranium?

indicators.note: looking into the following words is how the solver finds the letters sitting within them

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a particular garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is barely there: 'looking' doubles as part of the definition, and the question mark flags the letters sitting inside 'for a geranium'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who searches about for food or supplies is one who goes looking for things, plants included.

clue.text: Strong desire, at first, to urinate facing the other way

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is used
turned round, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: pee is the colloquial verb for urinating

explanation.surface: A desperate need for the toilet, best relieved while facing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing the other way' turns PEE into EEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep feelings or colours are intense, so the word works as a synonym for strong.

clue.text: This planet's evolving, not 50 years ago

indicators.note: evolving means changing form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means this letter is excluded from the fodder

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A remark on the Earth's change over time, excluding the last half-century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops L from THIS PLANETS, and 'evolving' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at an earlier time, long gone, which is what years ago says.

clue.text: Director of volunteers managed to get into trouble

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: The head of a volunteer group who managed to get into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' looks like the leader of volunteers, but it is a film-maker; 'trouble' rearranges INTO to TINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin, maker of Pulp Fiction, is a well-known film director.

clue.text: Graphical user interface needs department's manual

parts.note: GUI is the usual initialism for a graphical user interface
DE is the initialism of a Department of Education, as in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A department's software interface comes with an instruction book.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook of instructions is a guide, as in a user's handbook.

clue.text: Instrument for surveying Roman parts?

indicators.note: parts means only a portion of these words is used, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A query about the tool used to survey bits of the Roman world.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a Roman surveying tool, so the clue's surface is also apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-shaped surveying instrument used by Roman engineers to lay out straight lines.

clue.text: Steelyard demolished, not one to be converted again

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
not means the letter is left out

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An old steel works is pulled down, but one building is to be repurposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops A from STEELYARD; 'demolished' rearranges what is left. A steelyard is a balance for weighing.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new style is to remodel or convert it once more.

clue.text: Land what takes skill!

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the skill goes inside

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking someone to repeat what they said
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An exclamation: farming the land really requires expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil or ground is land, and the planet is also the land beneath our feet.

clue.text: Stop Dorothy holding Lion's tail or Tin Man's bottom

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy

indicators.note: the tail of the lion's name is its final letter, and the bottom of the word man would give the same letter

explanation.surface: Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz is told to stop grabbing her companions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is The Wizard of Oz, whose Dorothy travels with a Lion and a Tin Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperative telling someone to cease: the contraction means do not, so stop.

clue.text: Oversleep? I see alarm

parts.note: read as over plus sleep: sleep is nap, and over reverses it
the word see is pronounced like the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone realises they have overslept and panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversleep' splits into 'over', which turns NAP round to PAN, and 'sleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden fear or fright is a synonym for alarm.

clue.text: Launches campaigns

definitions.meaning: throws forward or propels, a verb in the third person
planned undertakings or schemes, a plural noun

explanation.surface: A headline about starting new drives or initiatives.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means throws forward; as a plural noun it means planned undertakings or schemes.

clue.text: In favour of Democrat president

parts.note: for means supporting, as in voting for
D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A voter backing a Democratic candidate for president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Democrat' misleads: Gerald Ford was a Republican, the 38th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th President of the United States, an example of a president.

clue.text: Fine cut of beef, finally to rescue from a stew

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to etch is to cut a design into a surface

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A recipe that cuts fine pieces of beef to save from a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: A stew here is a predicament; the phrase is an old expression for rescuing someone from a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrasal verb meaning to bring someone safely out of a difficulty or tight spot.

clue.text: Pasta made by a river over iron pan

indicators.note: over means turned over, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

indicators.note: a camera pans by swinging round, so these letters are swung into a new order

explanation.surface: Pasta cooked beside a river in an iron pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns A CAM into MACA; 'pan' rearranges IRON into RONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Short tubes of durum wheat dough are a classic type of pasta.

clue.text: King rat races against charioteer

indicators.note: races means runs about, so the letters dash into a new order

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the charioteer of the novel and film, giving the surname Hur

explanation.surface: A royal rat competes in a chariot race.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur, from the novel and film, is the charioteer; 'against' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary British monarch of Camelot and the Round Table was a king.

clue.text: Hard, long problem

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
to long for something is to have an itch for it

explanation.surface: A tough, lasting difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or temporary difficulty, as in going off without a hitch.

clue.text: Travellers welcome king and queens

parts.note: hi is a word of greeting or welcome
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
ER is the cipher of a queen, Elizabeth Regina, so queens are ERS

explanation.surface: Visitors are greeted by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Walkers on long country tramps are travellers on foot.

clue.text: Officially purchase novel via phone

indicators.note: a voice on the phone is heard, not read, so these words are judged by sound

parts.note: to purchase a novel is to buy the book

explanation.surface: Buying a novel over the telephone, done properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things according to the rules or proper procedure means doing them officially.

clue.text: Drink that's preferable for non-drinker to leave

indicators.note: to leave means these letters depart from the word

parts.note: better means preferable, more desirable
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A drink a teetotaller would rather leave alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale or lager is an alcoholic drink brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: Where shy women undress?

indicators.note: undressing removes outer garments, so each word loses its outside letters

explanation.surface: Asking where bashful women take their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undress' strips the outer letters of shy and women, leaving H and OME.
explanation.definitionFit: One's own dwelling is the place where, or a place to go; the definition is loose but the whole clue supports it.

clue.text: 1,001 computer expert tips on hand-held devices

parts.note: M is one thousand and I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the tips of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A huge number of tech experts give advice about handheld gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer pointing gadgets moved by the hand across a desk are devices held in the hand.

clue.text: Newspapers ditch leader to cover ultimate issues

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap round, so the other piece goes inside
ditching the leader removes the first letter

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
ult. is a recognised short form of ultimate

explanation.surface: Newspapers drop their editor to report on the most important matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' is abbreviated as in ult., a form used in old business letters; 'to cover' wraps the shortened press round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcomes or consequences are what something issues in; issues as a noun means results.

clue.text: Head of technology backs plastic-free PC monitor

indicators.note: backs means supports from behind, so this letter comes after the rest
plastic means pliable and mouldable, so these letters are remoulded
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tech boss promotes an eco-friendly computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monitor' looks like a computer screen but means a pupil with authority; 'plastic' rearranges FREE PC.
explanation.definitionFit: In schools a senior pupil given supervisory authority acts as a monitor.
